title: Imaging Mass Cytometry Data Acquisition
author: Michelle Daniel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf2ijqce
materials: 1. Attach the flat-bed scanner to a computer.
Under “Data acquisition” create a new Empty12AF file.

steps.title: Scan slides with flat‑bed scanner
steps.instruction: Use the flat‑bed scanner with the custom sample holder to scan up to 12 slides, saving each as a .jpg at 600 dpi.

substeps.instruction: Load up to 12 slides into the custom sample holder.
Scan the slides to .jpg at a resolution of 600 dpi and save the image.
Optionally perform a low‑resolution overview scan on any computer.

steps.title: Set up IMC acquisition
steps.instruction: Prepare the IMC instrument and data files before acquisition, creating panoramas that do not exceed 10 000 × 10 000 pixels.

substeps.instruction: Insert the slide into the IMC instrument.
In the “Data acquisition” menu, create a new file named Empty12AF.
Ensure the autofocus pins in the software are not positioned above the hydrophobic marker pen to avoid false focal planes and reduced ablation efficiency.
Save the resulting .mcd file on the data drive (E:) inside a newly created folder.
Create panorama images of the tissue sample, keeping each panorama ≤ 10 000 × 10 000 pixels; this requires a fully tuned, running IMC.

steps.title: Configure ROI and start acquisition
steps.instruction: Define regions of interest, load the appropriate panel, set acquisition parameters, and begin the IMC run.

substeps.instruction: Locate the areas of interest identified in the IHC staining within the panorama.
Set up an ROI for each region with a defined size (e.g., 1000 × 1000 pixels).
In AirLab, download the relevant panel (select “for CyTOF 2”) and save it to the folder containing the .mcd file.
Select all ROIs, go to “Template”, import the downloaded panel, scroll to the bottom of the list, and select the imported panel.
In the panel selection pane, set the ablation energy to 2.5 dB and the ablation frequency to 400 Hz.
Verify that the correct template is selected and that isotopes Ir191 and Ir193 are included.
Set the DV Opt parameter to 4 h.
Press “Start”. (Note: 1 mm² at 400 Hz should take roughly 1 h.)
